title: Signal Rosetta — E2E Latency Sleuth
content:
Purpose:
This note captures an experimental playbook and a set of working hypotheses for mapping noisy e2e latency signals to actionable root causes. The goal is a small, repeatable workflow (the "Rosetta") that converts trace+telemetry inputs into prioritized fixes for p50/p95/p99 regressions.

Summary of findings (top-line):
- Observed p50/p95/p99 regressions in the last 2 weeks are dominated by two distinct signal classes: (A) micro-batching queue spikes on certain route patterns, and (B) intermittent KV-cache miss storms correlated with cold-run GPU context changes.
- Typical per-request stage share at p99: queue_wait 46%, model_forward 31%, network_egress 12%, postprocess/serialize 8%, other noise 3%. At p50 the queue_wait share collapses to ~12% and model_forward dominates.

Why this is different: 
Instead of only looking at stage medians, Rosetta aligns per-trace heartbeat signals (batch size, KV hit flag, container-cold flag, seq_len) and computes a compact "signature" vector. Signatures are clustered and labeled; each cluster maps to a likely root cause. This compresses millions of traces into ~8 actionable phenotype buckets.

Instrumentation checklist used for these experiments:
- Trace spans: client_receive, request_enqueue, batch_enter, batch_exit, kv_lookup, model_infer_start, model_infer_end, emit_first_token, egress_send.
- Extra boolean tags: kv_hit, prewarm_flag, cold_gpu_context, route_id, seq_len_bucket.
- Sampling: stratified by route_id and seq_len_bucket; heavier sampling on routes with SLA misses.
- Dataset: 10k traces sampled across 48 hours (production), heavy tail preserved by oversampling p99 traces.

Raw aggregate numbers (sample set, 10k traces):
- p50 end-to-end: 86 ms
- p95 end-to-end: 213 ms
- p99 end-to-end: 512 ms

Representative per-stage breakdown (p50 / p95 / p99 median shares):
- tokenization: 4ms / 6ms / 9ms  (p50 share 5%, p99 share 2%)
- queue_wait (batcher): 10ms / 80ms / 236ms (p50 share 12%, p99 share 46%)
- kv_lookup: 2ms / 5ms / 18ms (kv-miss traces can spike to 60ms)
- model_forward: 60ms / 95ms / 160ms (larger seqlen & quantization fallback cause increases)
- emit-first-token latency (scheduling/serialize): 6ms / 15ms / 40ms
- egress/network: 4ms / 12ms / 38ms

Signature clustering result (8 phenotype buckets):
1) Small-queue steady (p50 workhorse): low queue_wait, kv_hit, short seq_len. Action: no-op.
2) Microburst queue spikes: short bursts where batcher accumulates 20–80ms unexpectedly; correlated with sudden route QPS bursts. Action: tune batch thresholds, enable burst-mode routing.
3) Cold GPU context + kv miss overlap: traces that have cold_gpu_context=true and kv_hit=false; model warmup + memory-stage causes long tail. Action: prewarm heuristics + pin hot models to warm instances.
4) Long-seq decode pressure: high model_forward; seq_len > 512. Action: route to larger-token-optimized kernels/instances.
5) Small QPS noisy network blips: egress dominant; correlated with a small subset of edge proxies. Action: add network retries and switch proxies.
6) Batch eviction contention: batch_enter-to-exit variance indicates eviction; often during infra maintenance windows. Action: change eviction policy; lower priority background work.
7) KV-store degradation: kv_lookup latency skew without cold_gpu. Action: instrument KV node health and add local LRU cache.
8) Mixed pathology: combination of microburst + kv-miss. Action: treat as high priority incident.

Example trace slices (anonymized):
- Trace A (p99): client_receive 0, request_enqueue 0ms->248ms (queue_wait 248ms), batch_enter 248ms, kv_lookup 5ms (miss=false), model_infer_start 258ms, model_infer_end 418ms (model_forward 160ms), emit_first_token 12ms, egress 32ms, total ~462ms. Signature => microburst cluster.
- Trace B (p99): request_enqueue 12ms, kv_lookup 62ms (kv_miss storm), model_forward 120ms, egress 26ms, total ~220ms. Signature => kv-miss cluster.

Hypotheses and quick experiments run: 
- Hypothesis 1: Batcher thresholds tuned for throughput create fragile behavior when route QPS has a heavy diurnal spike. Experiment: reduce max_hold_ms for that route from 100ms to 50ms and enable route-specific burst capacity. Result: p95 improved by ~18% for that route over 24h.
- Hypothesis 2: KV-store rebalances cause transient latency spikes matching our observed kv-miss storm. Experiment: temporarily disabled background compaction on the KV cluster during a test window. Result: observed reduction in kv_lookup tail (p99 -> p99.9) but at cost of increased memory usage.

Short-term mitigations (next 2 weeks):
- Deploy route-specific batcher knobs for top-10 customer routes (ENG-9472).
- Add a lightweight local in-memory LRU for KV responses with TTL=10s on model workers to blunt KV storming.
- Add an emergency prewarm flag the control plane can flip for flagged models during incidents.

Longer-term improvements (Q2):
- Implement signature-to-runbook mapping in Console: when a route hits p99, Console shows the top-3 candidate phenotype buckets and one-click actions (increase burst, prewarm, change kernel).
- Kernel-level telemetry add: per-attention-matrix time and per-layer offload signal. This requires minor changes to the runtime exporter.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need better separation of network egress skew vs. client-side TLS handshake delays; add a client-side echo trace to disambiguate.
- Evaluate whether lowering batch max_hold_ms universally increases average cost; need cost model experiment.
- Run the Rosetta on a 7-day sample to validate cluster stability and false-positive rate.

Action items and owners:
- Maya: roll-up the route-specific batcher change and schedule canary (PR drafted, see GitHub link).
- Oliver: prototype local LRU on model worker (branch: worker/local-kv-lru).
- Sofia: add signature visualization to the trace UI (mockups in Confluence).
- Rajiv: run 7-day Rosetta sweep and produce a follow-up report with confusion matrix for phenotype labels.

Appendix: quick reproducible commands (internal):
- sample traces for route X: internal-tool query-traces --route X --since 48h --stratify seq_len
- compute signatures: rosseta-cli compute-signatures --input traces.ndjson --out sigs.csv
- run cluster/visualize: pca + dbscan with min-samples=10 (notes in linked Confluence page).

Notes to self: this approach trades off complexity in cluster labeling for smaller operational surface when incidents happen. The Console integration is the decisive UX win — operators need the "top-3 causes" rather than a giant flamegraph.

If you poke at the sample traces linked above (JIRA ticket), you can see clear clusters of the queue_wait dominated traces that realigned with our microburst hypothesis. Keep an eye on model churn events; we've seen a recurring coincidence between model rollout windows and increased p99 tail.

End of draft.
